headlines.title: UC Berkeley student says she was followed, chased into her apartment complex
headlines.description: A UC Berkeley student said she was followed and chased into her off-campus apartment building on Tuesday night. Berkeley junior Eden Winograd said this all happened at around 8 p.m. on Tuesday when she was walking her dog near her off-campus apartment complex. That night, Winograd said she was walking her dog on the same path she does every night when she noticed a man approaching whom she had seen a few days earlier. “I started to panic a little bit, but I didn’t want to offend him if he was just standing there,” she said, recalling that she then started crossing the street. But then, she said the man started following directly behind her and saying things to her while she walked. “I started speeding up and heard his feet banging on the floor behind me,” she said. “I went up to the gate, I buzzed myself in, I went, and I closed it, and then I heard clanging sounds while I was walking inside, and I turned around, and he was like scaling the gate,” Winograd continued. “My heart sank, I was out of breath, my heart was pounding,” she recalled. She made it inside the elevator of her building before anything else happened, then called the police. Winograd posted the surveillance video of the incident on TikTok, where it has now been viewed more than 858,000 times. That surveillance video has now also been shared by Berkeley Police. The video shows Winograd walking into the gate of her apartment complex, walking her dog on a leash. A few seconds later, a man can be seen climbing over the same gate where she entered and following in the same direction Winograd walked in, holding something in his hand. Police said that initial reports indicated the suspect had a knife in his hand, but investigators later found that the object was likely a barbecue lighter. It is still unclear why that man would be holding a barbecue lighter. But for Winograd, that doesn’t change how alarming this incident was. “I don’t care if they have a weapon in their hand or nothing in their hand, I don’t want to be chased the second I step out of my apartment. I don’t want to be chased and have to watch someone claw their way up a wall to get to where I live,” she said. Police said that the following day, they were called about the same man lying on the sidewalk in the same area. Berkeley police said they detained him and confirmed he was involved in “the prior trespassing incident.” Police did not arrest that man, but they did send a case to the Alameda County District Attorney’s Office for review. Police have not released the man’s name, but they said he is 50 years old and experiencing homelessness.

headlines.title: Disabled train prompts major BART delay
headlines.description: A disabled train between the Fremont and Union City stations caused delays on the Berryessa line on Saturday, according to BART. At 12:15 p.m., BART said a disabled train between the Fremont and Union City stations was major causing delays on the Berryessa line. Just before 2 p.m., BART announced that train was cleared out of the way and it was in the process of restoring normal service, adding there was still a 20-minute delay on the Berryessa line in the Richmond, Daly City and Berryessa directions. headlines.title: More possible victims of man posing as 49ers player come forward, FBI says
headlines.description: The FBI says the number of women who say they were tricked online by a man posing as a 49ers player has grown to 61. Investigators are working to verify that the newly identified women are, in fact, victims of Daejon Love and Taylor Chan. Love and Chan are charged with several crimes including wire fraud. The FBI says Love posed as a 49ers player on dating apps to meet women online. He would then ask them for money for fake investments while Chan posed as his financial adviser, according to authorities. The FBI is asking anyone with information about Love or Chan to contact the agency.

headlines.title: Surveillance video shows moment ICE agent's gun found in San Francisco airport bathroom
headlines.description: Surveillance video from San Francisco International Airport obtained by NBC Bay Area is shedding more light on a July incident where an ICE deportation officer allegedly left his gun unattended in an airport restroom. A review of roughly two hours of CCTV footage – obtained through a California Public Records Act request – shows the moment the gun was found inside a bathroom stall by a flight attendant, along with the likely moment the ICE agent returned to the scene roughly 10 minutes later. As NBC Bay Area first reported in August, the firearm was found unattended inside a bathroom stall past security checkpoint D in Terminal 2, according to airport spokesperson Doug Yakel. Around 10:23 p.m., the surveillance video shows a person who appears to be the flight attendant run out of the bathroom and flag down airport security. The flight attendant and security officer then head back to the bathroom. Airport security then calls 9-1-1 and reports the gun to San Francisco police. “Hi, yeah, a flight attendant just came up to me and said there is a gun in the men’s bathroom,” an airport security officer tells police in a recording of the 9-1-1 call. San Francisco Aug 26 San Francisco Aug 27 The video shows additional law enforcement officers quickly arrive to investigate. Multiple travelers are turned away from the bathroom by police or security. The video makes it clear that dozens of people could potentially have found the gun if the flight attendant had not spotted it and notified security. Roughly 10 minutes after the flight attendant appears to discover the gun, the surveillance video shows a man dressed in plain clothes approach security outside the bathroom, present what looks like a badge, and enter the bathroom. The airport confirmed the man seen in the video was the ICE agent returning for his firearm. The video shows the apparent ICE agent emerge from the bathroom more than 10 minutes later with other law enforcement officials. He remains in front of the bathroom, where he seems to talk to officers on scene and present some sort of identification. Officers soon verify the gun belongs to the agent, according to police radio traffic. “We verified his firearm serial number through the government website,” someone says in the recording. Due to the position of the video camera and the quality of the video, it was not immediately clear to NBC Bay Area when the agent may have first left the gun in the bathroom. For weeks, NBC Bay Area has been asking ICE if the agent has faced any discipline for misplacing his gun, but the agency has not responded.
headlines.source: Hilda Gutierrez, Michael Bott and Alex Bozovic

headlines.title: Mountain lion released back into the wild after being captured in San Francisco
headlines.description: A young mountain lion was released back into the wild Friday after it was safely captured in San Francisco’s Sunset District. The mountain lion in the morning was spotted in yards and on a street. Video also showed the mountain lion on 44th Avenue. Neighbors said the animal moved from one bush to another in front of homes and stayed there. Police, animal control and other agencies responded. The street was blocked off and neighbors were told to stay back as officials worked to tranquilize the mountain lion. The California Department of Fish and Wildlife said the mountain lion was darted and ran off before the tranquilizer took effect. Officials then performed a quick health assessment and determined the animal was a male between 2 and 3 years old and weighed roughly 78 pounds. It was a morning that neighbors won’t soon forget. “It ran right in front of our house, and then they tranquilized it, and we saw it run out into the street too,” San Francisco resident Alex Grant said. “It was wild to see a mountain lion in a big city like this. It’s pretty incredible,” Grant added. Another neighbor, Carson Ryan, said he came to the area after seeing the police response. “I made my way over here at 10 o’clock. That’s when I saw all the police cars, caution tape, and I hung around and wanted to see what was really a mountain lion in the Outer Sunset, which it was,” Ryan said. After the mountain lion was safely captured, Fish and Wildlife officials placed a tracking collar on it and returned it to the wild. Officials said they are not sure where the mountain lion came from, but it could have traveled from the Peninsula, where there is habitat. headlines.title: Owners of Cupertino spa accused of running a brothel
headlines.description: The owners and the manager of a Cupertino spa were accused of running a brothel, the Santa Clara County District Attorney’s Office said on Thursday. The DA’s Office said 46-year-old Ling Wang and 48-year-old Xian Wang of San Jose have owned and operated the Hummingbird Day Spa since 2022, which offered sexual services to approximately 30 men daily. The brothel, according to authorities, brought in about $700,000 a year. The DA’s Office said it also charged the spa’s manager, 42-year-old Rui Wang of Sunnyvale. Officials said the investigation began in March, after reports of illegal sexual activity from the community. The DA’s Office said evidence showed that the business, marketed to male customers, had a high volume of men entering the facility over a short period of time every day. Further investigation revealed the Wangs were underreporting payroll by more than $100,000 per year, and that profits were funneled through mortgage payments to properties in San Jose and Chino Hills, along investments, according to authorities. The defendants were taken into custody on Sept. 10, according to the DA’s Office, and two women who were on the scene received support services from Community Solutions. Authorities added the defendants were charged with numerous felonies, including pimping and pandering, money laundering and tax and payroll fraud.

headlines.title: Another former FCI Dublin prison official charged in sex abuse case
headlines.description: Yet another correctional officer from a now-shuttered women’s prison in Dublin has been charged with sexually abusing inmates. On Wednesday, federal prosecutors filed five felony charges against David Perez, who was working as a disciplinary hearing officer at the notorious Federal Correctional Institution, Dublin. According to court filings, Perez allegedly abused two women, identified as R.M. and S.M., between August 2015 and December 2017. Using his authority as a prison official, Perez allegedly was able to get each woman alone with him in the prison’s “Captain’s Complex,” where he is accused of touching their breasts and buttocks and, on one occasion, “digitally penetrating” R.M.’s genitals, according to prosecutors. Perez is facing three counts of abusive sexual contact, one count of sexual abuse of a ward and one count of lying to federal investigators. If convicted of all charges, he could be sentenced to a maximum of 29 years in prison and could be on the hook for more than $1.2 million in fines. Perez has not been arrested and no lawyer is listed for him in court documents. He has not yet entered a plea or filed a response to the charges. In a related civil lawsuit filed on March 11 in federal court, R.M. says Perez allegedly routinely subjected her to sexual abuse and harassment. “In 2016, while she was housed in the SHU punishment cell following an altercation with another inmate, David Perez … began singling her out,” according to the suit. “Under the guise of addressing her disciplinary status, he summoned her alone, isolated her from others, pressed his body against hers, grabbed her by the hips, and groped her breasts and buttocks without her consent.” Perez allegedly engaged in similar behavior on at least four separate occasions, according to the suit. R.M. says she felt “frozen, terrified, and powerless to resist” because of Perez’s authority over her and she didn’t report the abuse because she feared retaliation, including the possible extension of her sentence. “The institutional culture within FCI Dublin created an environment of intimidation and coercion,” according to the lawsuit, which adds that the prison is “known for its culture of tolerating sexual misconduct.” In fact, Perez is the 11th official from the prison to be charged with sex-related offenses, including former warden Ray Garcia, who was convicted in 2022 and sentenced to nearly six years in prison. The former low-security prison closed in April 2024 in the wake of investigations into predatory sexual abuse of female inmates.

headlines.title: San Francisco security guards strike to demand better pay and benefits
headlines.description: Security guards across California are demanding higher wages and better benefits. On Friday, several hundred security guards held a one-day strike in San Francisco. San Francisco security guard Jakia Lane says she goes to work every day not knowing what danger she may face. “They want us to protect them, but they don’t want to protect us,” she said. “It is in the back of my mind, but I also try to keep situational awareness, so that I’m aware because you never know what somebody’s gonna do to you. These people can stab you, shoot you, walk up to you and shoot you, anything.” Lane and her fellow security guards say they don’t earn a living wage. Security guards staged a one-day strike in San Francisco today to demand better pay and benefits from the companies that employ them. “Right now, we’re looking at average pay between $22 and $23 an hour and we really think those are wages that are not going to be able to sustain families,” SEIU Union President David Huerta said. Huerta says guards deserve at least $30 an hour, better health and retirement benefits, and better training. But contract negotiations with their employers have stalled. The union has been negotiating with security contractors including Allied Universal, Securitas, GardaWorld and others for months. NBC Bay Area reached out to the security contractors and heard back from just one of them. Allied Universal says they’re focused on reaching an agreement saying, “We have made substantial progress in negotiations as part of our commitment to finding common ground.” Meanwhile, Lane says she’s juggling her guard duties with a second job as a hair stylist just to survive. She says she and her colleagues deserve better. The union says contract talks will resume on Tuesday. But they say if a deal isn’t reached, the picketing that took place in San Francisco could become widespread. “We could see strikes as early as next week in Los Angeles some of the biggest economic corridors, we could see strikes in the Silicon Valley. We could see strikes in the east Bay and most certainly here in San Francisco,” Huerta said.

headlines.title: Police investigate deadly shooting in Oakland
headlines.description: A man died following a shooting in Oakland on Friday, according to the police department. Police said the incident occurred shortly before 6 p.m. in the 1500 block of Magnolia Street. Authorities said they found a man with an apparent gunshot wound, who died at the scene. The police department said a suspect was arrested in connection with the incident, and the department’s Homicide Section is conducting a follow-up investigation into the circumstances surrounding the man’s death.

headlines.title: The Bernal Scream haunted house returns to San Jose
headlines.description: The Bernal Scream haunted house returned to San Jose Friday, and it’s bigger than ever. The homegrown haunt has nearly doubled its footprint this year to nearly 10,000 square feet. For the first time, it includes two main attractions: The Last Confession and Anxiety. The Last Confession takes visitors on a harrowing journey through their darkest sins. Anxiety is a psychological gauntlet designed to trigger primal phobias. The event also includes bouncy houses for younger children and glow-in-the-dark paintball. It opened its doors at 7:15 p.m. Friday and runs through Nov. 8.

headlines.title: CHP Solano catches driver sleeping inside Tesla going 60 mph
headlines.description: Solano CHP said Friday it caught a driver sleeping in his Tesla while going 60 miles an hour. The CHP says the driver thought he could hide the fact he was asleep behind dark sunglasses, but an officer spotted the driver slumping over. The CHP reminds everyone that self-driving features are meant to help but not replace drivers.
